source: Berkshire Museum: what is on view from reopening news and the architects’ press text; pictures from Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: Wally the Stegosaurus
artworks.description: The giant stegosaurus on the museum’s front lawn on South Street, a Pittsfield favourite; you pass him on the way in.
artworks.placeNote: Outside, on the front lawn on South Street.

artworks.title: The new lobby
artworks.description: The light-filled lobby of the 2026 renovation by StudioHAU (Los Angeles), with Bradley Architects of Pittsfield: ticket desk with an accessible counter, seats, coat racks, lockers and wheelchairs to borrow. The building opened in 1903, founded by the paper-mill owner Zenas Crane as a “Museum of Natural History and Art”, words still carved over the door.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Hall of History
artworks.description: The museum’s own story and Zenas Crane’s, with inventions and history from Pittsfield and the Berkshires: among them a painting of historic Wahconah Park, one of the oldest maps of Pittsfield, and art by Berkshire County students (the “Remembering Times Past” wall by Drury High School middle-schoolers).
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Feigenbaum Aquarium
artworks.description: Moved up from the basement in 2026 and twice its old size, the aquarium is now the heart of the first floor: five floor-to-ceiling tanks set like a cave, a lit glass walkway that looks like flowing water, and walk-through tunnels from the Hall of History and from Immersed in Nature. Next to the tanks live land animals (snakes, geckos, dart frogs, tortoises, a blue-tongued skink, a chameleon), fed partly by a hydroponic garden.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Caribbean reef octopus
artworks.description: Feigenbaum Aquarium. The photo shows the species, not the museum’s own animal. One of the new species since the 2026 reopening.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Moon jellyfish
artworks.description: Feigenbaum Aquarium. The photo shows the species, not the museum’s own animal. New since the 2026 reopening.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Bearded dragon
artworks.description: Feigenbaum Aquarium. The photo shows the species, not the museum’s own animal. New since the 2026 reopening.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Blue-tongued skink
artworks.description: Feigenbaum Aquarium. The photo shows the species, not the museum’s own animal. In the land-animal area beside the tanks.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Chameleon
artworks.description: Feigenbaum Aquarium. The photo shows the species, not the museum’s own animal. In the land-animal area beside the tanks.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Cabinets of Curiosities
artworks.description: Eight new red-oak cabinets inspired by Zenas Crane’s idea of a “window on the world”: weapons, jewellery, writing, paintings, musical instruments and natural history side by side, with drawers you can open and screens to explore. The objects change often, so curators can bring out more of the museum’s 40,000 things.
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Paleontology & Geology
artworks.description: Minerals, fossils, dinosaur bones and taxidermy in lit glass cases, with sculpture, paintings and scientific instruments among them, telling the story of the Earth before people.
artworks.galleryName: Paleontology & Geology (Gallery 3), with the glowing rock room
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.
artworks.imageCredit: photo of the fossil exhibit before the 2025–2026 renovation, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: The glowing rock room
artworks.description: A dark room in the middle of the Paleontology & Geology gallery, bigger than before, where minerals and objects made from them glow under special light. A favourite with children.
artworks.galleryName: Paleontology & Geology (Gallery 3), with the glowing rock room
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: The World in Miniature: Jonas Studios dioramas
artworks.description: Fourteen miniature wildlife scenes the museum ordered from Jonas Studios between 1946 and 1970, each showing a habitat somewhere in the world and its animals. Jonas Studios restored them for the 2026 reopening; the room has a globe in the middle and a fibre-optic star map of the night sky over Pittsfield.
artworks.galleryName: The World in Miniature: the Jonas Studios dioramas (Gallery 5)
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Immersed in Nature
artworks.description: Two galleries of the museum’s taxidermy in natural settings, with display cases, paintings and stones and fish native to Massachusetts. The selection changes from time to time.
artworks.galleryName: Immersed in Nature (Galleries 6 and 7), with the 360° room
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.
artworks.imageCredit: photo of a bird case before the 2025–2026 renovation, via Wikimedia Commons

artworks.title: Around the World 360
artworks.description: A round walk-in projection room that takes you to ten scenes around the globe, with sound; the museum plans to add Berkshire places such as the top of Mount Greylock.
artworks.galleryName: Immersed in Nature (Galleries 6 and 7), with the 360° room
artworks.placeNote: Where the architects’ plan puts this gallery.

artworks.title: Soulful Creatures: Animal Mummies in Ancient Egypt
artworks.description: A touring exhibition from the Brooklyn Museum’s Egyptian collection: mummified birds, cats, dogs and snakes with coffins, statues and amulets, and what they tell about how ancient Egyptians saw animals and the gods. In Galleries 206–208, through January 17, 2027.
artworks.placeNote: The museum lists the show in Galleries 206–208; where those rooms are on the second floor is approximate.

artworks.title: Ibis Coffin
artworks.description: Soulful Creatures: Animal Mummies in Ancient Egypt (Oct 10, 2026 – Jan 17, 2027), lent by the Brooklyn Museum. Brooklyn Museum 49.48a-b: a coffin for an ibis, the bird of the god Thoth, covered in silver and gold with rock-crystal eyes; it holds a simple ibis mummy. One of the touring show’s highlights.
artworks.placeNote: The museum lists the show in Galleries 206–208; where those rooms are on the second floor is approximate.

artworks.title: Objects and Their Stories
artworks.description: About 5,000 sq ft of the museum’s own art, science and history objects shown by theme, changing over time: Pittsfield Elm pictures and things carved from its wood, presidents’ portraits, musical instruments from around the world, animal skeletons.
artworks.placeNote: On the second floor since 2021; the room’s position on the map is approximate.

artworks.title: Pahat, the mummy
artworks.description: The museum’s Egyptian mummy, a visitor favourite, with an interactive display on Pahat’s journey from Egypt to the Berkshires.
artworks.placeNote: On the second floor since 2021; the room’s position on the map is approximate.

artworks.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace (cast)
artworks.description: A full-size cast of the Louvre’s Nike of Samothrace, brought into the museum through the roof in 1910 and moved “centimetre by centimetre” to this floor in 2021. The museum says it is not going anywhere again.
artworks.placeNote: On the second floor since 2021; the room’s position on the map is approximate.

artworks.title: Ellen Crane Memorial Room
artworks.description: The grand room named for Ellen Crane, used for shows and events; visitors pass through it on the way to Objects and Their Stories.
artworks.placeNote: On the second floor; the room’s position on the map is approximate.
